summary.title: The Internals of PostgreSQL
summary.one_liner: A free, chapter-by-chapter guide to how PostgreSQL's internal subsystems work, from heap tuples and query processing to the buffer manager, WAL, and replication.
takeaways: PostgreSQL is organized into cooperating subsystems, and understanding them helps with administration and integration.
Covered topics include database cluster and table layout, process and memory architecture, query processing, FDWs, and concurrency control.
Storage and maintenance chapters explain VACUUM, HOT updates, index-only scans, the buffer manager, and WAL.
Later chapters cover online backup, PITR, streaming replication, and logical replication (marked beta).
summary.summary: This is an online book by Hironobu Suzuki that explains how the internal subsystems of PostgreSQL work and gives an overall picture of the system. It is organized into 12 chapters plus sections, covering cluster and table structure, process and memory architecture, query processing, foreign data wrappers, concurrency control, VACUUM, HOT and index-only scans, the buffer manager, write-ahead logging, backup and PITR, and streaming and logical replication. The page states it covers versions 19 and earlier (excluding a new buffer page lock mechanism), and it has recent updates such as an asynchronous I/O section and a logical replication chapter. The page text is mostly the author's background and job-search notes, so the technical content is described only at the level of its chapter list.
